transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because I just can’t seem to settle down inside myself anymore. It feels like I need to get up and do the next thing, even when I’m exhausted and I know I should be sitting still.
When this happens, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do have nights where I don’t sleep well, but I haven’t noticed that I need a lot less sleep and feel fine. It’s more that I feel restless, not rested.
During these restless times, do you also feel unusually upbeat or high?
No, I don’t think so. I wouldn’t call it upbeat or high. It’s more like I’m wound up or unsettled, but not in a good mood or anything like that.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when you try not to?
I’m not sure I’d call it worrying a lot about different things. I do get unsettled, but I haven’t really noticed constant worry being the main thing.
Have you been using any drugs or stimulants lately, such as cocaine, methamphetamine, or nonprescribed ADHD medication?
No, not that I’m aware of. I haven’t been using things like that.
Did this unsettled, restless feeling start after something very stressful or traumatic happened?
Yes… I think it really started causing trouble after my husband died. That was about a year and ten months ago. Since then, I’ve felt this restless, unsettled way a lot more.
Do upsetting memories of your husband’s death come into your mind when you don’t want them to?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I think about him, of course, but I haven’t noticed memories of his death just pushing into my mind like that.
Before your husband died, did you already have this kind of restless, hard-to-settle feeling for many years, even going back to childhood?

Yes, I think so. Even back in grade school, my teachers would write things like I was bright but careless. I was always losing papers, talking when I shouldn’t, and needing reminders to stay in my seat or finish my work. So it wasn’t only after my husband died.
Do you often have trouble finishing tasks because your mind drifts or you get distracted?

Yes, that happens a lot. Like with the quilting charity, if someone gives me three or four things to do, I might start the first one right away, but then I drift off into some other chore. Before I know it, the last steps just don’t get finished.
Do you often blurt things out or interrupt other people before they finish speaking?

Yes. I do interrupt more than I mean to. In committee meetings especially, a thought will pop into my head and I just blurt it out because I’m afraid I’ll lose it, even if someone else is still talking. I don’t mean to be rude, but it happens.
Do these attention and interruption problems cause trouble for you in your day-to-day life?

Yes, it does. My family has had to step in with bills and paperwork because I let things pile up or miss something. And at church or with the garden group, people have had to redo plans or cover things I said I would handle and then didn’t follow through on. It’s embarrassing, honestly. These are people and groups I care about, and I can tell they don’t feel like they can count on me the way they used to.
Do these attention and interruption problems happen in more than one part of your life, such as at home and in groups or activities outside the home?

I’m not completely sure how to separate it out, but yes, I think it does show up in different places. It’s not just one setting. I notice it at home, and I also notice it when I’m with groups or helping with activities.
When you feel restless, is it usually because you’re feeling anxious?

Not always, no. Sometimes I’m anxious, but this feels more like I just can’t settle inside my own skin. I feel like I need to get up and do the next thing, even when I’m tired and I know I should just sit still.
Do these focus and restlessness problems interfere with your daily life?

Yes, it does. I’ve had trouble keeping up with bills and paperwork, so my family has had to step in. And with church and the garden group, I’ve dropped responsibilities or not followed through, and then other people had to redo plans or cover for me. It’s embarrassing, because these are people I care about, and I can tell they don’t feel they can rely on me like they used to.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things?
I’m not sure I’d say I worry about many different things all the time. I do worry about things that are right in front of me, but I haven’t really noticed it being constant worrying about everything.
Before you turned 12, were these attention and restlessness problems already happening?
Yes, it was. Even in grade school, teachers would say I was bright, but careless. I was always losing papers, talking when I shouldn’t, and needing reminders to stay in my seat or finish my work.
Do you avoid reminders of your husband’s death?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve noticed myself avoiding reminders on purpose. Some things are hard, of course, but I can’t say I go out of my way to avoid them.
Do you find yourself feeling jumpy or easily startled?
I don’t think so, not really. I mean, loud noises might make me look up like anyone, but I haven’t noticed being especially jumpy or startled all the time.
Do you ever have nightmares about your husband's death?
No, I don’t think I have nightmares about it. I may have bad dreams sometimes like anyone, but I haven’t noticed them being about my husband’s death.
